messages:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a rapid bakeoff this afternoon comparing bitsandbytes weight-only (bnb 8bit) vs llm.int8 on nova13b-v2 using our prod-like user-slice. posting notes here so we don't lose them
kevin: nice, link to raw results?
maria: uploaded CSV/logs: https://redwood.internal/bench/2475001234/results.csv 
kevin: thx
maria: command I used:
```
python run_bench.py --model nova13b-v2 --quant [bnb,llm.int8] --batch 1 --seq 512 --warmup 20 --iters 200
```
zara: short summary numbers?
maria: throughput (tokens/sec, avg over iters): bnb 39.2 t/s, llm.int8 44.7 t/s. latency p50/p95: bnb 22ms / 64ms, llm.int8 17ms / 78ms
sam: llm.int8 faster on avg but p95 hurts. any config differences?
maria: same config, same kernel stack. llm.int8 used grouped quant scales by default; bnb used per-tensor fallback where necessary. both on same GPU fleet (A100), same driver/kernel.
eval-bot: quality report attached: EM/ROUGE on our instruction-long slice vs fp16 baseline: bnb EM -0.8%, ROUGE-L -1.4%; llm.int8 EM -1.9%, ROUGE-L -3.2%
kevin: ugh that ROUGE hit for llm.int8 is ... large. where do errors concentrate?
maria: looked into slices — short Q/A and code-gen are mostly fine. long explanatory answers (400+ tokens) show divergence for llm.int8: hallucinations and repeated phrases. bnb looks more stable.
zara: can you paste a tiny example diff?
maria: sure — FP16 answer vs llm.int8 (truncated):
```
FP16: The 2018 policy introduced X, which reduced latency by 12% and affected Y.
llm.int8: The 2018 policy introduced Z, which increased latency and caused unrelated Y behavior. [hallucinated reference to study 'Smith 2017']
```
kevin: that sniff of invented refs is concerning. does bnb also hallucinate there?
maria: bnb occasionally, but much less often on same prompts. Skipped tokens and repetition were rare with bnb.
sam: any hypothesis? grouped scale granularity vs per-channel dynamic range?
maria: my current guess: llm.int8 aggressive grouping reduces representational fidelity in later layers where attention matrices have long-tail activations for these long-context instructions. that manifests as coherent drift after ~350 tokens.
zara: can we try a hybrid profile: llm.int8 default but keep last N layers in fp16 or bnb?
maria: tried last 4 layers in fp16 (mixed profile) — throughput dropped ~7%, p95 improved, EM delta narrowed: llm.int8+hYbrid EM -1.1% vs fp16. not as good as full fp16 but better than pure llm.int8.
eval-bot: perf numbers for hybrid: throughput 41.6 t/s, p50 19ms, p95 58ms.
kevin: nice tradeoff. does that map to an easy rollout policy? maybe route longform requests to hybrid profile?
sam: we could also auto-fallback when token length > 350 or when prompts hit certain eval slices. routing/rollout work in console would be trivial to implement as a per-route policy.
maria: agreed. I also ran a quick GPTQ-style post-quantization (small per-channel correction) patch on llm.int8 and saw EM improve by ~0.4% but throughput dropped 3-4% due to extra ops.
zara: action items?
maria: 1) mark llm.int8 as fast-but-risky for longform; 2) create a hybrid profile (last-4-fp16) as fallback; 3) add a slice-based guardrail rule in Console to route longform prompts or >350 tokens to hybrid; 4) follow-up notebook to test grouped-scale granularity tweaks (A/B). I'll open tickets.
kevin: please include short example prompt set and the CSV in the ticket. also add a note about the hallucination pattern (invented refs) so eval team can create targeted slices.
maria: will do. thanks all. :sparkles:
